Generate multiple-response (select-all-that-apply) values

Source: R/misc.R
fkr_multiple_response.Rd

Simulates a "select all that apply" survey item: each generated value is one or more entries from values combined together, e.g. with values = LETTERS[1:4] a result might be "A", "AC", or "ABCD". Selected entries always keep their original order from values (so "AC" can occur but "CA" cannot), and never repeat within a single generated value.

Usage

fkr_multiple_response(n, values, multiple = TRUE, sep = "")

Arguments

n

Number of values to generate. A single non-negative whole number.

values

A non-empty vector of candidate entries, with no NAs, to combine (e.g. LETTERS[1:4], or option labels like c("Email", "Phone", "SMS")).

multiple

If TRUE (default), each generated value may combine more than one entry from values. If FALSE, exactly one entry is drawn per value, as in a single-response ("select one") item.

sep

String used to join multiple selected entries together. Default "", which reads naturally when values are single characters (e.g. "AC"); for multi-character values, pass something like sep = ", " to keep entries distinguishable (e.g. "Email, SMS").

Value

A character vector of length n.

Details

The number of entries selected for each value is drawn uniformly from 1:length(values) (not uniformly over all non-empty subsets), so picking exactly 1 entry is just as likely as picking all of them.

Examples

fkr_multiple_response(5, values = LETTERS[1:4])
#> [1] "ABC" "C"   "BD"  "ABC" "D"  
fkr_multiple_response(5, values = c("Email", "Phone", "SMS"), sep = ", ")
#> [1] "Email, Phone" "Email"        "SMS"          "Email, Phone" "SMS"         
fkr_multiple_response(5, values = LETTERS[1:4], multiple = FALSE)
#> [1] "A" "B" "A" "A" "C"
